notes.heading: Overview
points: Governor is the constitutional head of a State
Acts as the nominal executive, while real power lies with the Council of Ministers
Functions similar to the President at the state level
Provided under Part VI of the Constitution (Articles 153–167)

notes.heading: Constitutional Position
points: Governor is the head of the state executive
All executive actions are taken in his/her name
Acts on aid and advice of Council of Ministers
Important link between Centre and State

notes.heading: Appointment of Governor
points: Appointed by the President of India
Holds office during the pleasure of the President
Usually appointed from outside the state

notes.heading: Qualifications
points: Must not be a member of Parliament or State Legislature
Must not hold any office of profit

notes.heading: Conditions of Office
points: Cannot be a member of legislature
Emoluments cannot be reduced during tenure

notes.heading: Term of Office
points: Holds office at the pleasure of the President
Can be removed before completion of term

notes.heading: Oath or Affirmation
points: Administered by Chief Justice of High Court
Swears to preserve, protect, and defend the Constitution

notes.heading: Executive Powers
points: Appoints Chief Minister and Council of Ministers
Appoints Advocate General, State Election Commissioner
Administers state affairs in his/her name

notes.heading: Legislative Powers
points: Summons, prorogues, and dissolves State Legislature
Promulgates ordinances when legislature not in session

notes.heading: Financial Powers
points: No money bill can be introduced without Governor’s recommendation
Ensures annual budget is laid before legislature

notes.heading: Judicial Powers
points: Can grant pardons, reprieves, respites, or remissions
Appoints district judges (in consultation with High Court)

notes.heading: Discretionary Powers
points: Can act without advice of Council of Ministers in certain situations
Appointment of CM in hung assembly
Report to President for President’s Rule (Article 356)

notes.heading: Role as Agent of Centre
points: Acts as a link between Union and State
Reports to President about state affairs

notes.heading: Criticism of Office of Governor
points: Seen as agent of Centre rather than neutral authority

notes.heading: Conclusion (UPSC Perspective)
points: Governor is a key constitutional authority at state level
Plays dual role: constitutional head and Centre’s agent
Balance between neutrality and political reality is crucial

notes.heading: Important Constitutional Articles
points: Article 163: Council of Ministers to aid and advise

notes.heading: Important UPSC Points
points: Important link between Centre and State

notes.heading: Overview
points: Governor is not elected but appointed
Represents the Union at the State level
Ensures smooth functioning of constitutional machinery
Important aspect of Indian federal structure

notes.heading: Constitutional Provision
points: Article 155: Governor shall be appointed by the President
Article 156: Holds office during the pleasure of the President
No direct or indirect election involved

notes.heading: Mode of Appointment
points: Appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal
In practice, President acts on advice of Union Council of Ministers
Ensures coordination between Centre and State

notes.heading: Qualifications (Recalled)
points: Must not hold office of profit
Must not be a member of Parliament or State Legislature

notes.heading: Oath Before Appointment
points: Administered by Chief Justice of High Court

notes.heading: Conventions Followed in Appointment
points: Governor is usually from outside the state
Not actively involved in local politics

notes.heading: Why Appointment (Not Election)?
points: Avoids conflict between Governor and elected State Government
Ensures unity and integrity of nation

notes.heading: Term Related to Appointment
points: But serves at pleasure of President

notes.heading: Removal of Governor
points: Can be removed by President anytime
Based on advice of Union Government

notes.heading: Conclusion (UPSC Perspective)

notes.heading: Overview
points: Conditions of office define the rules and restrictions applicable to the Governor
Ensure independence, neutrality, and proper functioning
Provided mainly under Article 158 of the Constitution
Prevent conflict of interest and misuse of position

notes.heading: Constitutional Provision
points: Article 158 deals with conditions of Governor’s office
Ensures dignity and independence of office

notes.heading: No Membership of Legislature
points: Governor cannot be a member of Parliament or State Legislature
If a member is appointed, he/she must resign

notes.heading: No Office of Profit
points: Governor cannot hold any other office of profit

notes.heading: Emoluments (Salary and Allowances)
points: Governor is entitled to salary, allowances, and privileges
Paid from Consolidated Fund of the State

notes.heading: No Reduction During Tenure
points: Salary and allowances cannot be reduced during term

notes.heading: Official Residence
points: Governor is entitled to official residence (Raj Bhavan)

notes.heading: Immunities and Privileges
points: Governor enjoys legal immunity for official acts
Cannot be answerable to any court for official actions

notes.heading: Multiple States Governor
points: Same person can be appointed Governor of two or more states
Seen in practice in several instances

notes.heading: Restrictions on Conduct
points: Should not engage in active politics
Must act on aid and advice of Council of Ministers

notes.heading: Conclusion (UPSC Perspective)
points: Conditions of office safeguard dignity and neutrality

notes.heading: Important Constitutional Article
points: Related to salary, restrictions, and privileges

notes.heading: Overview
points: The term of the Governor defines the duration for which he/she holds office
It reflects both constitutional provisions and practical political realities
Important topic for understanding Centre-State relations

notes.heading: Constitutional Provision
points: Article 156 deals with the term of the Governor
Provides both fixed term and flexibility
Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President
Creates a dual nature of tenure

notes.heading: Normal Term
points: Governor holds office for a term of 5 years
Term begins from the date of entering office
However, not an absolute or guaranteed tenure
Subject to pleasure of the President

notes.heading: Doctrine of Pleasure
points: Governor holds office at the pleasure of the President
Can be removed at any time without assigning reasons
Based on advice of Union Council of Ministers

notes.heading: Continuation Beyond Term
points: Governor continues in office even after 5 years until successor takes charge

notes.heading: Transfer of Governor
points: Governor can be transferred from one state to another

notes.heading: Issues and Criticism
points: Governor seen as agent of Centre

notes.heading: Supreme Court View
points: Removal cannot be arbitrary or capricious
Judicial review possible in limited cases

notes.heading: Reform Suggestions
points: Sarkaria Commission: fixed tenure of 5 years

notes.heading: Conclusion (UPSC Perspective)
points: Term is nominally 5 years but practically flexible
Balance between flexibility and stability is needed

notes.heading: Important Constitutional Article
points: Pleasure of President is key concept

name: Powers and Features of the Governor

notes.heading: Overview
points: Governor is the constitutional head of the State
Exercises various powers similar to the President at the Union level
Works on aid and advice of Council of Ministers except in certain cases
Combines constitutional authority with limited discretionary role

notes.heading: Executive Powers
points: Appoints Chief Minister and other ministers
Appoints Advocate General and State Election Commissioner
All executive actions taken in his/her name

notes.heading: Legislative Powers
points: Summons, prorogues, and dissolves State Legislature
Addresses first session after elections and each year
Can withhold or reserve bills for President
Promulgates ordinances when legislature is not in session

notes.heading: Financial Powers
points: No Money Bill can be introduced without Governor’s recommendation
Controls contingency fund of the state

notes.heading: Judicial Powers
points: Can grant pardons, reprieves, respites, or remissions
Applies to offences against state laws
Appoints district judges in consultation with High Court

notes.heading: Discretionary Powers
points: Acts without advice of Council of Ministers in certain cases
Appointment of CM in hung assembly

notes.heading: Key Features of the Office
points: Dual role: State head + Agent of Centre

notes.heading: Governor as Agent of Centre
points: Reports to President regarding state affairs

notes.heading: Limitations on Powers
points: Bound by aid and advice of Council of Ministers
Subject to judicial review in some cases

notes.heading: Issues and Criticism
points: Seen as instrument of central government

notes.heading: Conclusion (UPSC Perspective)
points: However, role is mostly ceremonial in normal circumstances
Discretionary powers make the office important in crises
Balance between neutrality and political reality is crucial

notes.heading: Important UPSC Points
points: Discretionary powers are key for prelims

advanced.question:
Consider the following:
1. Governor has executive powers
2. Governor issues ordinances
3. Governor is real executive
Which of the following is NOT correct?

notes.heading: Overview
points: Governor is the constitutional head of the State
Occupies a position similar to the President at the Union level
Acts as a nominal executive while real power lies with the Council of Ministers
Key figure in maintaining constitutional governance in the State

notes.heading: Nominal vs Real Executive
points: Governor is the nominal (de jure) executive
Chief Minister is the real (de facto) executive
All executive actions are taken in the name of the Governor
Actual decisions are made by Council of Ministers

notes.heading: Aid and Advice Principle
points: Governor acts on aid and advice of Council of Ministers
Ensures parliamentary system at state level

notes.heading: Discretionary Powers Exception
points: Governor can act independently in certain situations
Examples: appointment of CM in hung assembly
These powers create practical importance of office

notes.heading: Governor as Agent of Centre
points: Acts as representative of the Union government
Reports to the President on state affairs
Acts as a link between Centre and State

notes.heading: Dual Role of Governor
points: This dual role creates both importance and controversy

notes.heading: Position in State Executive
points: Executive power of the State vested in Governor (Article 154)
Governor is head of state administration

notes.heading: Comparison with President
points: Both act on aid and advice
President has more defined discretionary limits
Governor has relatively wider discretionary role in practice

notes.heading: Limitations of Position
points: Bound by advice in most matters
Subject to judicial review in some cases

notes.heading: Issues and Controversies
points: Seen as agent of central government
Frequent debates on role in federalism

notes.heading: Supreme Court View
points: Governor must act within constitutional limits
Judicial review possible in certain cases

notes.heading: Conclusion (UPSC Perspective)
points: Governor is a nominal head but constitutionally significant
Dual role makes the office unique in Indian federalism
Real power lies with elected government
Proper use of discretion is key to maintaining balance
